### HTML scraping

Yes. We examined whether including webpage header content could improve the prediction of claims status. We modified the text extraction process to include HTML heading elements (h1–h6) in addition to paragraph text. The results showed that including header information improved the ROC AUC from 0.841 to 0.873. This improvement suggests that webpage headings contain useful information for identifying claims-related content and can enhance predictive performance.

### Bigrams

We investigated whether bigrams capture additional information relevant to claims classification beyond individual words. We first created bigram features from the webpage text, applied stopword removal and lemmatization, and selected the 2,000 most frequent bigrams. We then used principal component analysis to reduce the dimensionality of the bigram features. A ridge-regularized logistic PCR model was fitted to the word-tokenized data to obtain predicted log-odds, which were combined with the bigram principal components in a second logistic regression model.

The Word-only model achieved a test ROC AUC of 0.857, while the combined Word + Bigram model achieved 0.850. The decrease of approximately 0.007 indicates that adding bigram features did not improve predictive performance. Therefore, our results provide no clear evidence that bigrams capture additional useful predictive information beyond individual words.


### Neural net

Architecture: We developed a neural network with a text vectorization layer that converted webpage text into TF-IDF features, followed by a dropout layer, one hidden dense layer with 64 units and ReLU activation, another dropout layer, and a sigmoid output layer. The vocabulary was limited to 6,000 tokens.

Optimization and loss: The model was optimized using the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 0.001 and binary cross-entropy as the loss function. We also applied a dropout rate of 0.6 and L2 regularization of 0.001 to help reduce overfitting.

Training epochs: The final model was trained for 30 epochs with a batch size of 32.

Predictive accuracy: On the test data, the final neural network achieved a ROC AUC of approximately 0.836, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.797–0.875. Its classification accuracy was 78.5%.
